source: Franceschelli and Musolesi (2024) On the Creativity of Large Language Models (Boden's definitions, as relayed)
finding: Boden defines creativity as ideas or artefacts that are new, surprising and valuable. Three kinds of surprise map to three types: combinational (unfamiliar combinations of familiar ideas), exploratory (new options inside the current style of thinking), transformational (changing the style of thinking). Boden's own book was NOT opened; this is a secondary restatement.
numbers: Definitions only. Cites Boden 2003/2004 The Creative Mind.
quote: Combinatorial creativity involves making unfamiliar combinations of familiar ideas.
limits: Primary Boden text not read. The paper reads the types as surprise at rising levels of abstraction.
agent_relevance: Gives the vocabulary for S3 open mode: three different generator jobs (recombine, search inside a space, change the space's rules).

source: Franceschelli and Musolesi (2024) On the Creativity of Large Language Models (P- vs H-creativity)
finding: Boden separates P-creativity (new to the producer) from H-creativity (new in all history). The paper adds 'B-novelty' (new to the beholder) and argues LLM output often looks creative only in the B sense.
numbers: No empirical numbers. Conceptual argument.
limits: Argument paper; no measurement. B-novelty is the authors' own coinage.
agent_relevance: Warns that ideas a user finds 'new' may only be B-novel. Supports G8: novelty must be checked against prior work, not felt.

source: Franceschelli and Musolesi (2024) On the Creativity of Large Language Models (verdict on LLM types)
finding: Authors argue current LLMs can reach at most combinational or exploratory creativity. Transformational creativity is called not achievable through current training because of autoregressive fit to the data distribution and RLHF/DPO alignment that lowers diversity.
numbers: No experiment. Cites Kirk et al. 2024 on lower diversity after alignment.
quote: Transformational creativity is not achievable through the current LLM training solutions.
limits: A theoretical claim, not tested. Scaffolds such as Universe of Thoughts (a11-a14) partly contest it by simulating rule change in the prompt.
agent_relevance: Says the model alone will not change its own space; the program must force the rule change. Fits 'program decides, model fills a slot'.

source: Espirito Santo, Wiggins, Cardoso (2024) Towards a Formal Creativity Theory (Wiggins CSF as relayed)
finding: Wiggins' Creative Systems Framework has three rule sets: R defines the boundary of the conceptual space, T generates artefacts in an ordered sequence, E picks artefacts with value. Exploratory creativity moves inside a space under R, T, E. Transformational creativity is changing the rule set itself.
numbers: Wiggins 2006 is described through this later paper; the 2006 Knowledge-Based Systems paper itself could not be opened (publisher page only).
quote: Wiggins paraphrases Boden's transformational creativity as 'transforming the rule set'.
limits: Second-hand. Wiggins 2006 and Boden 1990/2004 primary texts not read this session.
agent_relevance: Mapping to our schema: R = task constraints in the prompt, T = the generator, E = the code check. A transformation step changes R, not just the sample.

source: Espirito Santo, Wiggins, Cardoso (2024) Towards a Formal Creativity Theory (formal learning theory)
finding: Recasts a conceptual space as a recursively enumerable set; the inspiring set is what the agent has seen; novelty = artefact not in the inspiring set; transformativeness = the agent changes its hypothesis as experience grows. Proves novelty is neither necessary nor sufficient for transformational creativity over experience sequences, but is required if the agent holds only an unordered inspiring set.
numbers: Theorem-based, no data. Definitions 10-16 (conceptual space, inspiring set, schema, novelty VN, transformativeness VTr).
limits: Preliminary paper; authors say only some properties are defined and computability is open. Value is 0/1 only.
agent_relevance: Novelty is relative to what the agent was shown. Keep an explicit seen-set and test novelty against it in code.

source: Schapiro, Black, Varshney (2025) Transformational Creativity in Science: A Graphical Theory (formal model)
finding: Models a scientific conceptual space as a directed acyclic graph of constraints. Sink nodes are axioms; other nodes are rules that depend on them. Transformation = adding or removing edges or vertices. Proves that changing axioms has the greatest transformative potential, since all dependents inherit the change.
numbers: Case table: Ptolemaic to heliocentric, Newtonian to relativistic physics, Euclidean to non-Euclidean geometry (altered parallel postulate). No empirical test.
limits: Short ICCC paper; proofs and cases only, no quantitative validation. Science only.
agent_relevance: Concrete operator: list the assumptions the current approach rests on, rank them by number of dependents, and flip the root ones first. Candidate for O4/O6/O8.

source: Schapiro, Black, Varshney (2025) Transformational Creativity in Science: A Graphical Theory (lineage claims)
finding: Lists the lineage: Wiggins (2006) treats transformational creativity as exploratory search over the space of generative systems; Ritchie (2006) stresses changes to the structure of the space; Toivanen et al. (2018) use meta-level modules that change the constraints of a song search; Espirito Santo et al. (2024) use learning theory.
numbers: Citation map only.
limits: Relays others' views. Not independent confirmations of one result.
agent_relevance: Shows the shared computational reading: transformation = meta-level search over constraints.

source: Shahhosseini et al. (2026) LLMs for Scientific Idea Generation: A Creativity-Centered Survey (Boden used as lens)
finding: Survey sorts LLM idea methods by Boden level: recombination methods -> combinatorial, systematic exploration -> exploratory, assumption challenging -> possibly transformational. States most methods reach the combinatorial or exploratory level, transformational remains elusive, and evaluation is the main bottleneck.
numbers: No single number; TMLR 02/2026.
quote: These assignments are conceptual ,reflecting tendencies rather than guaranteed outcomes.
limits: Authors' own assignment of methods to types, not validated by raters.
agent_relevance: A map of generators by type; a prior for choosing the S3 generator.

source: Shahhosseini et al. (2026) LLMs for Scientific Idea Generation: A Creativity-Centered Survey (search and test-time scaling)
finding: Reports that tree search lifts ideation reward: Tree-of-Thought 9.91-13.8 over hundreds of candidates (NP=253, depth 5); Monte Carlo Thought Search 12.47-15.6 (NP about 301, depth 9). Reads this as exploratory creativity bought with compute, bounded by evaluator quality and one model's distribution.
numbers: Rewards quoted from a cited prompt-search study; ranges as given.
limits: Numbers come from another study, not run by the survey. Cost rises with depth.
agent_relevance: Deeper search buys exploratory coverage but needs a non-model scoring signal (G8, G12).

source: Shahhosseini et al. (2026) LLMs for Scientific Idea Generation: A Creativity-Centered Survey (multi-agent claim)
finding: Says multi-agent debate could approach transformational creativity but marks this as speculative. Cites VirSci: human novelty 3.78 vs 3.10-3.22 for single agents, feasibility 5.24 vs 4.78-4.94; and the Google AI co-scientist rediscovering an unpublished bacterial gene-transfer mechanism.
numbers: VirSci human ratings as quoted; co-scientist is one case.
limits: Speculative; one in-silico rediscovery, not a controlled test. Conflicts with our G9 (no debate); gain may be extra sampling.
agent_relevance: Do not adopt debate on this evidence; log as contested.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani (2026) Universe of Thoughts (design)
finding: Turns Boden's three modes into three executable search programs for an LLM: C-UoT transfers structure from distant analogue problems; E-UoT expands neighbouring candidates with the rules fixed; T-UoT proposes rule changes and keeps only those that preserve the task and its core difficulty. The rule-change filter is part of T-UoT.
numbers: Three new low-constraint tasks (Bridge, Electricity, Society) plus HypoArena (100 hypothesis tasks: 34 bio, 34 ML, 32 social).
limits: Authors' own operationalisation. v3 dated 6 Oct 2026.
agent_relevance: A ready blueprint for three S3 generators, with the filter that stops 'change' becoming noise.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani (2026) Universe of Thoughts (low-constraint tasks, GPT-4o, 10 generations per method)
finding: T-UoT best on Bridge and Electricity (human creativity 0.680 and 0.620 vs OnePrompt 0.480 and 0.540; CoT 0.590 and 0.560; ToT 0.580 and 0.530). On Society no method clearly wins (C-UoT 0.560, EGoT 0.560, OnePrompt 0.550, T-UoT 0.550). E-UoT scored 0.430 on Electricity, below OnePrompt.
numbers: Creativity = mean of novelty and utility; 10 PhD students plus Gemini 2.5 Pro as LLM judge (T-UoT LLM scores 0.698, 0.526, 0.628).
limits: Only 10 generations per cell. Human and LLM scores disagree (Electricity: LLM top is T-UoT 0.526 but CoT only 0.450 vs human 0.560). No confidence intervals shown.
agent_relevance: The rule-change generator helps when the goal is specific and the space is loose; do not use it where constraints are tight.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani (2026) Universe of Thoughts (HypoArena, Qwen3-14B)
finding: On 100 scientific hypothesis tasks E-UoT ranks first: average rating 1535.4, pairwise win rate 32.7% vs 25.5% for the next best (ToT 1515.8). T-UoT is sixth (1484.6; WR 17.3%), C-UoT fifth (1489.6; WR 19.5%), plain OnePrompt last (1475.7; WR 14.3%). With GLM-4-9B, OnePrompt ranked first.
numbers: Gemma-3-12B judge; two other judges preserve E-UoT's edge over OnePrompt and ToT (agreement 0.59-0.79; hard reversals 2.6-5.4%).
limits: Judge is an LLM (G8 concern). Result flips with the backbone (GLM-4-9B). Constrained, high-specificity tasks favour local exploration.
agent_relevance: For constrained problems use exploratory search first; transformation and analogy are not reliable there.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani (2026) Universe of Thoughts (operator ablation and failure modes)
finding: Removing the Boden-specific operator costs: full C-UoT preferred in 58.3% of paired comparisons, T-UoT 54.2%, E-UoT 52.4% (chance 50%). Failure analysis: C-UoT finds good analogies but loses the mechanism in final synthesis; T-UoT finds rule changes but does not carry the consequences into the answer. Fixing this on frozen failure cases moved a T-UoT rank from #7 to #2.5.
numbers: 100 HypoArena tasks, position-debiased pairwise LLM judge.
limits: Effects are small (2-8 points over chance) and LLM-judged; the frozen-case fix is a diagnostic on selected cases.
agent_relevance: Weak point is carrying a transformed rule's consequences forward: let code or a check propagate them instead of trusting one pass.

source: Sun et al. (2025) OMEGA: Can LLMs Reason Outside the Box in Math?
finding: OMEGA (40 template generators, six math domains) tests three axes after Boden: exploratory (same skill, harder instance), compositional (combine two skills learned apart), transformative (a different, unconventional strategy needed). Four frontier reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, o3-mini, o4-mini) lose accuracy sharply as complexity rises; 100 items per level.
numbers: Exact-match accuracy; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Math-7B fine-tuned with GRPO on 1k problems.
limits: 'Compositional' is the authors' middle axis (close to Boden's combinational); 'transformative' means a strategy shift in math, not a rule-space change. Templated tasks.
agent_relevance: A code-checked probe for the exploratory vs transformative gap that we could reuse.

source: Sun et al. (2025) OMEGA: Can LLMs Reason Outside the Box in Math? (RL results by type)
finding: RL lifts exploratory generalization: Zebra Logic base 30%, +61 points in-distribution and +53 out-of-distribution. Compositional: skills trained alone reach strong accuracy (often above 69%; polygon rotation 13% base, about +70 points) but the combined problem gains little (about +6 pp; GCD plus polynomial roots none). Transformative: out-of-distribution accuracy stays low, often 0%; the one notable gain is +10 pp (Setting 7), still via naive solutions; matrix rank fell 30 points from a 70% base.
numbers: 1k training problems, GRPO, 7B models; RL needs non-zero base accuracy.
limits: Small models only; may not transfer to frontier models. Training on levels 1-4 instead of 1-2 raised level 3 only from 6% to 10%.
agent_relevance: Training moves a model along strategies it has; only a scaffold that forces a different strategy can reach beyond. Test against held-out strategy-shift items.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench
finding: Code-generation benchmark for combinatorial (Combo) and exploratory (Explore) creativity. Creativity score = quality x novelty; quality by sandboxed tests, novelty as logic distance to baselines. Gemini-3-Pro Pass@1 under 60% on both subsets. Human experts judged 89.1% of instances valid; automated creativity rankings agree with human ones at Spearman 0.78.
numbers: Mean over N=10 runs; three master's students verified data.
limits: Novelty = code-logic distance; correctness is separate from value. Covers two of Boden's three types (no transformational).
agent_relevance: A code-checked novelty metric exists that avoids model judges (G8); reusable idea for our selector.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench (scaling and convergence)
finding: Scaling helps combination more than exploration: Gemini-3-Pro improves combinatorial creativity while exploratory creativity slightly declines. 'Convergence-by-scaling': larger models raise Pass@1 while novelty falls or plateaus, so the creativity score rises mainly from correctness. Reasoning ability helps constrained exploration more than combination.
numbers: Claims from the paper's text and figures; the compression explanation is the authors' hypothesis.
limits: The explanation is untested. Code tasks only.
agent_relevance: A bigger model is more correct but less divergent. For S3 open mode, diversity must come from the scaffold, not from model size.

source: Wang et al. (2026) CreativeBench (EvoRePE steering)
finding: Training-free steering vector built from evolutionary-search prompt pairs. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Combo: AlphaEvolve creativity 0.175 -> 0.193 with EvoRePE; Pass@1 10.81% -> 11.48%. Paired tests over 10 seeds: Combo Pass@1 +0.80 pp (95% CI 0.68-0.92), Combo creativity +0.020, Explore Pass@1 +0.60 pp, Explore creativity +0.0012.
numbers: Absolute Explore creativity is tiny (about 0.015-0.018 for the 7B model).
limits: Gains are small; needs white-box activations; unusable on API-only models.
agent_relevance: Not applicable to a prompt-only scaffold; noted so we do not chase it.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE)
finding: KOMBINE tests association, analogy and blending across 35 LLMs and 75 humans. LLMs are 10-16 points better at association and analogy than at blending. Valid association 59.0%, valid analogy 53.4%, valid blend 43.4% (LLM mean); humans 22.1%, 32.9%, 12.8%. Given a valid shared abstraction, models write a coherent blend 97.1% of the time.
numbers: Three-judge LLM panel; panel agrees with a human 75% of the time when unanimous (n=96), 66% for majority.
limits: Text only; judges are LLMs; one model (gpt-5.6-sol) reverses the pattern (64.8% blending vs 55.4% analogy).
agent_relevance: The weak step in combination is finding the shared abstraction, not writing the blend. Add an explicit step that names the generic space.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE) (homogeneity)
finding: One in five invented concepts (412 of 2,070) reuses a property another model invented. Models are 14x more likely to reuse on blends than on analogies, and 2.3x more likely when from the same provider. Humans and LLMs reach different regions of semantic space.
numbers: Reuse measured at a similarity threshold; provider effect 2.3x.
limits: Reuse depends on the threshold and embedding model.
agent_relevance: Samples from one model are not independent ideas (G4); mix providers or human input if real spread is wanted in S3.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE) (Boden background)
finding: Appendix: exploratory = artefacts that follow the space's rules (AlphaGo move 37 as the example); transformational = restructuring the rules (relativity, heliocentrism, non-Euclidean geometry; plot twists in fiction). Notes that psychometric tests built for humans show poor external validity on LLMs (Schapiro et al. 2026a).
numbers: Citations only; TwistBench (Schapiro et al. 2026b) is cited but was not opened.
limits: Relays citations; TwistBench not read.
agent_relevance: Do not trust human creativity tests to rate our agent.

source: Colton, Cook, Hepworth, Pease (2014) On Acid Drops and Teardrops: Observer Issues in Computational Creativity
finding: Defines computational creativity as software that unbiased observers would deem creative. Says a bias against computer-made artefacts has been seen under experimental conditions, and argues Turing-style comparison tests make this worse.
numbers: Position paper; case studies of an automated painter and generated games. No sample figures taken.
limits: Opinion paper; I read only the opening pages.
agent_relevance: Evaluate creative output with checks, not blind human-vs-machine comparisons.

source: Fanelli (2026) The next Fourier transform: rewiring, representation, and artificial mathematical creativity
finding: Cites Boden's explore-vs-transform distinction as precedent and proposes a 'Rewiring Thesis': a conceptual revolution is a persistent, large-scale reorganisation of which problems can inform each other. Case: vibrating string (d'Alembert, Bernoulli, Euler, Lagrange, then Fourier).
numbers: Historical case with stress tests (Galois, Riemann, Lebesgue-Schwartz, Wiles); no measures.
limits: Conceptual; single main case.
agent_relevance: A test for 'did we transform?': does the new frame let methods move between problems that shared none before.

source: Gangloff (2026) Assessing LLMs' mathematical abilities requires understanding the various mechanisms of mathematical creativity
finding: Argues concept creation (a new stable primitive, close to Boden's transformational) is the recurring bottleneck, while recombination mechanisms already cover combinational and exploratory creativity. Claims competence in one mode will not transfer to the others.
numbers: Position paper; no data.
limits: Opinion without measurement.
agent_relevance: Matches the survey view; treat as hypothesis, not result.

source: Yu, Ahn, Romero (2026) Dataset repurposing and disruptive AI research
finding: Study of AI papers: most repurposed datasets gain little short-term visibility, yet repurposing is associated with more disruptive work and, when later adopted, higher citation impact. Authors read this as support for transformational creativity theory (a dataset used for a new question opens a new space). Repurposing teams are more experienced and academia-industry mixed, but team traits poorly predict adoption.
numbers: Regression models; specific coefficients not recorded here.
limits: Observational and correlational; mapping 'repurposing' onto Boden's transformation is the authors' interpretation.
agent_relevance: Real-world hint that reusing a tool for a different question tends to give disruptive work: a prompt of the form 'what else could this be used for?'.

source: Boriceanu and Dinu (2026) Creative Transformation in Literary Texts: Modelling Change Across Representational Levels
finding: Frames creativity as selective transformation of a predecessor across lexical, semantic, conceptual, structural and narrative levels, with similarity calibrated against controls. Recalls early computational creativity as search over rule-governed spaces (Boden 2004; Wiggins 2006).
numbers: Pairs of historically documented literary relationships; no headline figure recorded.
limits: Small corpus of canonical works; results are interpretive profiles.
agent_relevance: A way to measure how much an idea keeps from its source vs changes, level by level; possible novelty check.

source: Wikipedia (2026) Computational creativity (reading of Boden and Wiggins)
finding: Names Boden's exploratory and transformational creativity, calling transformational 'far more radical, challenging, and rarer'. Notes Wiggins (2006) as the main formalisation of Boden's insights, in Knowledge-Based Systems.
numbers: Citation lists only (Boden 1990, 1999, 2009; Wiggins 2006; Ritchie 2009).
limits: Encyclopedia summary; no numbers.
agent_relevance: Confirms the lineage Boden to Wiggins that the SUBFIELDS row cites.
